verses.1:1: The word of the LORD that came to Hosea son of Beeri in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, the kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, the king of Israel.
verses.1:2: At the beginning, when the LORD spoke through Hosea, the LORD said to Hosea, "Go, take for yourself a wife of prostitution and children of prostitution, for the land utterly prostitutes itself, departing from the LORD."
verses.1:3: He went and took Gomer daughter of Diblaim, and she conceived and gave birth to a son for him.
verses.1:4: Then the LORD said to him, "Call his name Jezreel, for in just a little while I will call the house of Jehu to account for the bloodshed of Jezreel, and I will bring the kingdom of the house of Israel to an end.
verses.1:5: And it will happen on that day that I will break the bow of Israel in the Valley of Jezreel."
verses.1:6: Then she conceived again and gave birth to a daughter. And He said to him, "Call her name Lo-ruhamah, for I will no longer show compassion to the house of Israel, that I should ever pardon them.
verses.1:7: Yet to the house of Judah I will show compassion, and I will save them by the LORD their God; I will not save them by bow, sword, or war, nor by horses or horsemen."
verses.1:8: Then she weaned Lo-ruhamah, and she conceived and gave birth to a son.
verses.1:9: And He said, "Call his name Lo-ammi, for you are not My people, and I will not be yours."
verses.2:1: Yet the number of the sons of Israel will be like the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured and cannot be numbered. And it will happen that in the place where it is said to them, "You are not My people," it will be said to them, "Sons of the living God."
verses.2:2: And the sons of Judah and the sons of Israel will gather together, and they will set one head for themselves and go up from the land, for the day of Jezreel will be great.
verses.2:3: Call your brothers "Ammi" and your sisters "Ruhamah."
verses.2:4: Contend against your mother, contend, for she is not My wife, and I am not her husband; let her remove her prostitution from her face and her adultery from between her breasts,
verses.2:5: or else I will strip her naked and expose her as on the day of her birth, and I will make her like the wilderness, set her like a parched land, and put her to death with thirst.
verses.2:6: And to her children I will not show compassion, for they are children of prostitution.
verses.2:7: For their mother has prostituted herself; the one who conceived them has behaved shamefully. For she said, "I will go after my lovers, the givers of my bread and my water, my wool and my flax, my oil and my drinks."
verses.2:8: Therefore, look, I am about to hedge up your way with thorns, and I will erect a wall against her so that she will not find her paths.
verses.2:9: She will eagerly pursue her lovers, yet she will not catch up with them; she will seek them, yet she will not find them. Then she will say, "I will go and return to my first husband, for it was better for me then than it is now."
verses.2:10: Yet she did not know that I Myself gave her the grain, the new wine, and the fresh oil, and multiplied silver and gold for her, which they used for Baal.
verses.2:11: Therefore I will return and take My grain in its time and My new wine at its appointed season, and I will snatch away My wool and My flax meant to cover her nakedness.
verses.2:12: And now I will expose her indecency before the eyes of her lovers, and no one will rescue her from My hand.
verses.2:13: And I will bring all her rejoicing to an end: her feast, her new moon, her Sabbath, and every appointed festival of hers.
verses.2:14: And I will devastate her vine and her fig tree, of which she said, "They are my wages that my lovers gave me." I will turn them into a forest, and the wild animals of the field will devour them.
verses.2:15: And I will call her to account for the days of the Baals, when she would burn incense to them, adorned herself with her ring and her jewelry, and went after her lovers, yet she forgot Me, declares the LORD.
verses.2:16: Therefore, look, I am going to allure her, lead her into the wilderness, and speak to her heart.
verses.2:17: And I will give her her vineyards from there, and the Valley of Achor as a doorway of hope; and she will answer there as in the days of her youth, and as on the day she went up from the land of Egypt.
verses.2:18: And it will happen on that day, declares the LORD, that you will call out, "My husband," and you will no longer call Me "My Baal."
verses.2:19: And I will remove the names of the Baals from her mouth, and they will no longer be remembered by their name.
verses.2:20: And on that day I will make a covenant for them with the wild animals of the field, and with the birds of the heavens and the creeping things of the ground; I will break bow, sword, and war from the land, and I will cause them to lie down in safety.
verses.2:21: And I will betroth you to Me forever; I will betroth you to Me with righteousness and with justice, with loyal love and with compassion.
verses.2:22: And I will betroth you to Me with faithfulness, and you will know the LORD.
verses.2:23: And it will happen on that day that I will answer, declares the LORD; I will answer the heavens, and they will answer the earth;
verses.2:24: and the earth will answer the grain, the new wine, and the fresh oil, and they will answer Jezreel.
verses.2:25: And I will sow her for Myself in the land, and I will show compassion to Lo-ruhamah; and I will say to Lo-ammi, "You are My people," and he will say, "My God."
verses.3:1: Then the LORD said to me, "Go again, love a woman who is loved by a companion and is an adulteress, just as the LORD loves the sons of Israel, even though they turn to other gods and are lovers of raisin cakes."
verses.3:2: So I bought her for myself for fifteen shekels of silver, a homer of barley, and a lethech of barley.
verses.3:3: Then I said to her, "For many days you must remain for me; you must not prostitute yourself, and you must not belong to any man; and I too toward you."
verses.3:4: For the sons of Israel will remain many days without king and without prince, without sacrifice and without pillar, and without ephod or teraphim.
verses.3:5: Afterward, the sons of Israel will turn back and seek the LORD their God and David their king, and they will come in trembling to the LORD and to His goodness in the latter days.
verses.4:1: Hear the word of the LORD, sons of Israel, for the LORD has a dispute with the residents of the land, because there is no truth, no loyal love, and no knowledge of God in the land.
verses.4:2: Cursing, lying, murdering, stealing, and committing adultery—they break out, and bloodshed touches bloodshed.
verses.4:3: Therefore the land mourns, and everyone dwelling in it wastes away, together with the wild animals of the field and the birds of the sky, and even the fish of the sea are swept away.
verses.4:4: Yet let no one dispute, and let no one rebuke, for your people are like those who dispute with a priest.
verses.4:5: You will stumble by day, and a prophet will also stumble with you by night; and I will bring your mother to ruin.
verses.4:6: My people are brought to ruin for lack of knowledge. Because you have rejected knowledge, I will reject you from serving as priest to Me; and since you have forgotten the instruction of your God, I too will forget your children.
verses.4:7: As they grew numerous, so they sinned against Me; I will exchange their glory for disgrace.
verses.4:8: They eat the sin of My people, and each one sets his appetite on their iniquity.
verses.4:9: And it will be the same for the people as for the priest; I will call them to account for their ways and bring their deeds back upon them.
verses.4:10: They will eat, yet not be satisfied; they will engage in prostitution, yet not increase, because they have abandoned heeding the LORD.
verses.4:11: Prostitution, wine, and new wine take away discernment.
verses.4:12: My people inquire of their piece of wood, and their staff declares to them; for a spirit of prostitution has led them astray, and they have engaged in prostitution, departing from under their God.
verses.4:13: On the summits of the mountains they offer sacrifices, and on the hills they burn incense, under oak, poplar, and terebinth, because their shade is good. Therefore your daughters engage in prostitution, and your daughters-in-law commit adultery.
verses.4:14: I will not call your daughters to account when they engage in prostitution, nor your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery, for they themselves go aside with prostitutes and offer sacrifices with shrine prostitutes; and a people who do not understand will be thrown down.
verses.4:15: Though you engage in prostitution, Israel, let Judah not incur guilt; do not come to Gilgal, do not go up to Beth-aven, and do not swear, "As the LORD lives."
verses.4:16: For like a stubborn heifer, Israel has been stubborn; will the LORD now shepherd them like a lamb in an open pasture?
verses.4:17: Ephraim is bound to idols; let him be.
verses.4:18: Once their liquor is gone, they continually engage in prostitution; her rulers deeply love disgrace.
verses.4:19: A wind has bound her up in its wings, and they will be put to shame because of their sacrifices.
verses.5:1: Hear this, priests; pay close attention, house of Israel; and house of the king, give ear! For the judgment is against you, because you have been a snare for Mizpah and a net spread out over Tabor.
verses.5:2: And the rebels have plunged deep into slaughter, yet I am a discipline for all of them.
verses.5:3: I know Ephraim, and Israel is not concealed from Me; for now you have engaged in prostitution, Ephraim; Israel is defiled.
verses.5:4: Their deeds do not let them return to their God, because a spirit of prostitution is within them, and they do not know the LORD.
verses.5:5: Israel's pride testifies to his face; Israel and Ephraim will stumble in their iniquity; Judah too has stumbled with them.
verses.5:6: With their flocks and with their herds they will go to seek the LORD, yet they will not find Him; He has drawn away from them.
verses.5:7: They have betrayed the LORD, for they have borne alien children; now a new moon will devour them together with their allotments.
verses.5:8: Blow the ram's horn in Gibeah, the trumpet in Ramah! Sound the alarm in Beth-aven! Behind you, Benjamin!
verses.5:9: Ephraim will become a wasteland on the day of rebuke; among the tribes of Israel I have made known what is certain.
verses.5:10: The officials of Judah have become like those who shift a boundary; upon them I will pour out My fury like water.
verses.5:11: Ephraim is oppressed, crushed by judgment, because he resolved to walk after a precept.
verses.5:12: So I am like a moth to Ephraim, and like decay to the house of Judah.
verses.5:13: When Ephraim saw his illness and Judah his wound, Ephraim went to Assyria and sent to King Jareb; yet he is not able to heal you, nor will he cure your wound.
verses.5:14: For I am like a lion to Ephraim and like a young lion to the house of Judah. I, yes I, will tear apart and go away; I will carry off, and there is no one to rescue.
verses.5:15: I will go and return to My place until they admit their guilt and seek My face; in their distress they will diligently seek Me.
verses.6:1: "Come, and let us return to the LORD, for He is the one who has torn us apart, and He will heal us; He has struck us, and He will bind us up.
verses.6:2: He will restore us to life after two days; on the third day He will raise us up, and we will live in His presence.
verses.6:3: And let us know, let us pursue knowing the LORD: as certain as the dawn is His coming forth, and He will come to us like the rain, like the spring rain that soaks the earth."
verses.6:4: What am I to do with you, Ephraim? What am I to do with you, Judah? For your loyal love is like a morning cloud, and like the dew that departs early.
verses.6:5: Therefore I have hewn them down by the prophets; I have killed them by the words of My mouth, and your judgments are like light going forth.
verses.6:6: For I take pleasure in loyal love and not sacrifice, and in the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.
verses.6:7: But they, like Adam, have violated the covenant; there they have betrayed Me.
verses.6:8: Gilead is a city of those who work wickedness, marked with bloody footprints.
verses.6:9: And as bands of raiders lie in wait for a man, a company of priests murders along the road to Shechem, for they have practiced depravity.
verses.6:10: In the house of Israel I have seen an appalling thing: Ephraim's prostitution is there; Israel is defiled.
verses.6:11: For you too, Judah, a harvest has been set, when I restore the fortunes of My people.
verses.7:1: Whenever I would heal Israel, the guilt of Ephraim is laid bare, and the wicked acts of Samaria, for they practice falsehood; a thief comes in, and a troop raids outside.
verses.7:2: And they do not say to their heart that I remember all their wickedness. Now their deeds surround them; they are before My face.
verses.7:3: With their wickedness they make a king glad, and with their lies, officials.
verses.7:4: All of them are adulterers, like an oven set burning by a baker, who stops stoking from the kneading of the dough until it is leavened.
verses.7:5: On the day of our king, the officials grew sick with heat from wine; he stretched out his hand with mockers.
verses.7:6: For they have brought their heart near like an oven in their ambush; all night their baker sleeps; in the morning it blazes like a flaming fire.
verses.7:7: All of them grow hot like an oven and devour their judges. All their kings have fallen; not one among them calls to Me.
verses.7:8: Ephraim mixes himself among the peoples; Ephraim has become a flat cake not turned over.
verses.7:9: Foreigners have devoured his strength, and he does not know; gray hair as well is sprinkled over him, and he does not know.
verses.7:10: And Israel's pride testifies to his face, yet they have not returned to the LORD their God, nor have they sought Him despite all this.
verses.7:11: And Ephraim has become like a gullible dove, devoid of sense; to Egypt they call, to Assyria they go.
verses.7:12: As they go, I will spread My net over them; like the birds of the sky I will bring them down. I will discipline them according to the announcement to their assembly.
verses.7:13: Woe to them, for they have wandered from Me! Destruction to them, for they have rebelled against Me! I would redeem them, yet they have spoken lies against Me.
verses.7:14: And they do not cry out to Me with their heart, but instead they wail on their beds; for grain and new wine they gather together; they turn against Me.
verses.7:15: I Myself trained and strengthened their arms, yet against Me they plot evil.
verses.7:16: They turn, but not upward; they are like a treacherous bow. Their officials will fall by the sword because of the rage of their tongue; this will be their mockery in the land of Egypt.
verses.8:1: Put the horn to your mouth! Like an eagle over the house of the LORD, because they have violated My covenant, and against My law they have rebelled.
verses.8:2: To Me they cry out, "My God, we, Israel, know You!"
verses.8:3: Israel has spurned what is good; an enemy will pursue him.
verses.8:4: They have installed kings, yet not from Me; they have appointed officials, yet I did not know. With their silver and their gold they have made idols for themselves, so that it may be cut off.
verses.8:5: He has spurned your calf, Samaria! My anger blazes against them. How long will they be unable to attain innocence?
verses.8:6: For it too is from Israel; a craftsman made it, and it is not God. Surely the calf of Samaria will become splinters.
verses.8:7: For wind they sow, and a whirlwind they will harvest. It has no standing grain; the sprout yields no flour; even if it should yield, foreigners will swallow it up.
verses.8:8: Israel has been swallowed up; now they are among the nations like a vessel in which there is no pleasure.
verses.8:9: For they themselves have gone up to Assyria, a solitary wild donkey by itself; Ephraim has hired lovers.
verses.8:10: Even if they hire among the nations, now I will gather them together, and they will start to grow few under the burden of the king of officials.
verses.8:11: Because Ephraim has multiplied altars for sinning, they have become to him altars for sinning.
verses.8:12: Though I write for him the many things of My law, they are counted as something foreign.
verses.8:13: As for the sacrifices of My offerings, they sacrifice meat and eat it, yet the LORD does not accept them. Now He will remember their guilt and punish their sins; they themselves will return to Egypt.
verses.8:14: Israel has forgotten his Maker and built palaces, and Judah has multiplied fortified cities; so I will send fire into his cities, and it will devour her citadels.
verses.9:1: Do not rejoice, Israel, to the point of exultation like the peoples, for you have prostituted yourself, forsaking your God; you have loved a prostitute's wage on all threshing floors of grain.
verses.9:2: Threshing floor and winepress will not feed them, and new wine will fail her.
verses.9:3: They will not dwell in the land of the LORD, but Ephraim will return to Egypt, and in Assyria they will eat what is unclean.
verses.9:4: They will not pour out wine to the LORD, nor will they be pleasing to Him; their sacrifices will be to them like bread of mourning. All who eat it will become unclean, for their bread is for their own appetite; it will not enter the house of the LORD.
verses.9:5: What will you do for the day of the appointed assembly, and for the day of the LORD's feast?
verses.9:6: For look, they are gone because of destruction; Egypt will gather them, Memphis will bury them. As for the precious things of their silver, nettles will take possession of them; thorns will be in their tents.
verses.9:7: The days of reckoning have come, the days of repayment have come; Israel will know! The prophet is a fool; the man of the spirit is mad, because of the greatness of your guilt, and great is the hostility.
verses.9:8: The watchman over Ephraim is with my God; as for the prophet, a fowler's snare is on all his ways, and hostility is in the house of his God.
verses.9:9: They have sunk deep in corruption, as in the days of Gibeah; He will remember their guilt; He will punish their sins.
verses.9:10: Like grapes in the wilderness I found Israel; like an early fig on a fig tree in its first season I saw your fathers. Yet they came to Baal-peor and consecrated themselves to the shameful thing, and they became detestable things like what they loved.
verses.9:11: Ephraim—like a bird their glory will fly away: no childbirth, no womb, and no conception.
verses.9:12: Even if they raise their children, I will bereave them until not a person is left; yes, woe to them as well when I depart from them!
verses.9:13: Ephraim, just as I saw concerning Tyre, is planted in a meadow; yet Ephraim must bring out his children to the killer.
verses.9:14: Give them, LORD—what will You give? Give them a miscarrying womb and dried-up breasts.
verses.9:15: All their wickedness is in Gilgal, for there I hated them. Because of the evil of their deeds, from My house I will drive them out. I will no longer love them; all their officials are rebels.
verses.9:16: Ephraim is struck down; their root has dried up; they will yield no fruit. Even if they give birth, I will put to death the precious ones of their womb.
verses.9:17: My God will reject them, for they have not listened to Him, and they will become wanderers among the nations.
verses.10:1: Israel is a spreading vine; he puts forth fruit for himself. According to the abundance of his fruit, he multiplied altars; according to the goodness of his land, they made fine standing stones.
verses.10:2: Their heart is deceitful; now they will bear guilt. He Himself will demolish their altars; He will devastate their standing stones.
verses.10:3: For now they will say, "There is no king for us, because we did not fear the LORD; and the king, what would he do for us?"
verses.10:4: They speak words, swearing false oaths, making covenants; so judgment blossoms like poison-weed along the furrows of the field.
verses.10:5: The inhabitants of Samaria will be in dread over the calves of Beth-aven; for its people mourn over it, and its idol-priests wail over it, over its glory, because it has gone into exile from it.
verses.10:6: It too will be carried to Assyria as tribute to King Jareb; Ephraim will receive disgrace, and Israel will be ashamed of his counsel.
verses.10:7: As for Samaria, her king is cut off like a splinter on the surface of the water.
verses.10:8: And the high places of Aven, the sin of Israel, will be destroyed; thorn and thistle will spring up over their altars. Then they will say to the mountains, "Cover us!" and to the hills, "Fall upon us!"
verses.10:9: From the days of Gibeah you have sinned, Israel; there they have remained. Will war against the sons of unrighteousness not overtake them at Gibeah?
verses.10:10: At My desire I will discipline them, and peoples will be gathered against them when they are bound for their two iniquities.
verses.10:11: Ephraim is a trained heifer loving to thresh, and I passed over her fine neck; I will hitch up Ephraim, Judah will plow, Jacob will harrow for himself.
verses.10:12: Sow for yourselves toward righteousness; reap according to the measure of loyal love. Break up unplowed ground for yourselves, for it is time to seek the LORD, until He comes and showers righteousness upon you.
verses.10:13: You have plowed wickedness; you have reaped unrighteousness; you have eaten the fruit of deception, for you trusted in your way, in the abundance of your mighty men.
verses.10:14: So an uproar will arise among your people, and all your fortresses will be devastated, just as Shalman devastated Beth-arbel on the day of battle, when a mother was dashed to pieces along with children.
verses.10:15: Thus Bethel will do to you because of the evil of your wickedness; at dawn the king of Israel will be utterly cut off.
verses.11:1: When Israel was a boy, I loved him, and from Egypt I called My son.
verses.11:2: As they called to them, so they went away from them; they kept sacrificing to the Baals and burning incense to the carved images.
verses.11:3: Yet it was I who taught Ephraim to walk; He took them up in His arms, but they did not know that I healed them.
verses.11:4: With human cords I drew them, with bands of love; I became to them like those who lift up a yoke from their jaws, and I bent down to him and fed him.
verses.11:5: He will not return to the land of Egypt, but Assyria itself will be his king, because they refused to return.
verses.11:6: A sword will whirl through his cities, put an end to his diviners, and devour them because of their schemes.
verses.11:7: And My people cling to turning away from Me; though they summon him to the Most High, not one at all will exalt Him.
verses.11:8: How could I give you up, Ephraim, deliver you over, Israel? How could I make you like Admah, set you like Zeboiim? My heart turns over within Me; all at once My compassions are stirred.
verses.11:9: I will not carry out My burning anger; I will not return to destroy Ephraim; for I am God, not a man, the Holy One in your midst, and I will not come in fury.
verses.11:10: They will follow after the LORD; like a lion He will roar. Indeed, He Himself will roar, and sons will come trembling from the west.
verses.11:11: They will come trembling like a bird from Egypt and like a dove from the land of Assyria, and I will cause them to dwell in their houses, declares the LORD.
verses.12:1: Ephraim has surrounded Me with deception, and the house of Israel with deceit; Judah still roams unruly against God, against the faithful Holy One.
verses.12:2: Ephraim herds the wind and pursues the east wind; all day long he multiplies falsehood and devastation. They make a covenant with Assyria, and oil is carried to Egypt.
verses.12:3: The LORD also holds a dispute with Judah, and He will call Jacob to account according to his ways; according to his deeds He will pay him back.
verses.12:4: In the womb he grasped his brother by the heel, and in his vigor he struggled with God.
verses.12:5: He struggled with an angel and prevailed; he wept and pleaded with Him for favor. At Bethel He found him, and there He spoke with us,
verses.12:6: Even the LORD, the God of hosts—the LORD is His renown.
verses.12:7: So as for you, return to your God; keep loyal love and justice, and wait always for your God.
verses.12:8: A trader—in his hand are scales of deceit; he loves to defraud.
verses.12:9: And Ephraim said, "Indeed, I have grown rich; I have found wealth for myself. In all my toil they will not find in me any iniquity that is sin."
verses.12:10: Yet I am the LORD your God from the land of Egypt; once more I will cause you to dwell in tents, like the days of the appointed festival.
verses.12:11: And I spoke to the prophets; I Myself multiplied visions, and by the hand of the prophets I delivered parables.
verses.12:12: If Gilead is iniquity, surely they have become nothingness. In Gilgal they have sacrificed bulls; their altars too will be like stone heaps along the furrows of the field.
verses.12:13: Now Jacob fled to the country of Aram; Israel worked for a wife, and for a wife he kept watch.
verses.12:14: And by a prophet the LORD brought Israel up out of Egypt, and by a prophet he was watched over.
verses.12:15: Ephraim has provoked bitter anger; therefore He will leave his bloodguilt upon him, and his Lord will pay back his reproach to him.
verses.13:1: When Ephraim spoke, there was trembling; he lifted himself up in Israel, yet he became guilty through Baal and died.
verses.13:2: And now they go on sinning and make for themselves a cast image from their silver, idols according to their skill, all of it the work of craftsmen. About them they say, "Those who sacrifice humans kiss calves."
verses.13:3: Therefore they will be like a morning cloud and like the dew that departs early, like chaff whirled from a threshing floor and like smoke from a window.
verses.13:4: Yet I am the LORD your God from the land of Egypt; you are to know no God besides Me, and there is no savior apart from Me.
verses.13:5: I Myself knew you in the wilderness, in a land of drought.
verses.13:6: According to their pasture they were satisfied; they were satisfied, and their heart grew lofty; for that reason they forgot Me.
verses.13:7: So I have become to them like a lion; like a leopard along the road I will keep watch.
verses.13:8: I will confront them like a bear bereaved of her cubs, and I will tear open the enclosure of their heart; and I will devour them there like a lioness; a wild beast of the field will rip them open.
verses.13:9: It has ruined you, Israel, because you are against Me, against your helper.
verses.13:10: Where then is your king, that he may save you in all your cities, and your judges, about whom you said, "Give me a king and officials"?
verses.13:11: I give you a king in My anger, and I take him away in My fury.
verses.13:12: Ephraim's iniquity is bound fast; his sin is stored away.
verses.13:13: The pangs of a woman in labor come upon him; he is an unwise son, for when it is time he does not take his stand at the mouth of the womb.
verses.13:14: Should I ransom them from the hand of Sheol? Should I redeem them from death? Where are your plagues, Death? Where is your destruction, Sheol? Compassion will be hidden from My eyes.
verses.13:15: Though he flourishes among brothers, an east wind will come, the wind of the LORD rising from the wilderness; and his fountain will dry up, and his spring will be parched. It will plunder the storehouse of every prized article.
verses.14:1: Samaria will bear guilt, because she has rebelled against her God; they will fall by the sword, their young children will be dashed to pieces, and its pregnant women will be ripped open.
verses.14:2: Return, Israel, to the LORD your God, for you have stumbled through your iniquity.
verses.14:3: Take words with you and return to the LORD. Say to Him, "Forgive all iniquity and accept what is good, so that we may offer our lips as bulls.
verses.14:4: Assyria will not save us; we will not ride on horses, and we will no longer say 'Our God' to the work of our hands, for in You the orphan receives compassion."
verses.14:5: I will heal their turning away; I will love them freely, for My anger has turned away from him.
verses.14:6: I will be to Israel like the dew; he will blossom like the lily and strike his roots like Lebanon.
verses.14:7: His shoots will reach out, and his splendor will be like the olive tree, and he will have fragrance like Lebanon.
verses.14:8: Those who dwell in his shadow will return; they will grow grain and blossom like the vine; his renown will be like the wine of Lebanon.
verses.14:9: Ephraim, what more have I to do with idols? I Myself have answered and will watch over him. I am like a flourishing cypress; from Me your fruit is found.
verses.14:10: Who is wise? Let him understand these things, and let the discerning one know them. For the ways of the LORD are straight, and the righteous walk in them, yet transgressors stumble in them.

notes.1:2: The opening clause places a construct noun directly before a finite Piel verb (tehillat dibber-YHWH, literally "the beginning of the LORD spoke"); the preposition be- ("through") can also mean "with" or "to."
notes.1:6: Lo-ruhamah means "She has not been shown compassion" (Pual perfect of raham, echoing the Piel verb "show compassion"). The closing clause (ki naso essa lahem, literally "that forgiving I should forgive them") carries forward the preceding negation ("I will no longer"), though some take ki adversatively as "but I will surely take them away."
notes.1:9: Lo-ammi means "Not My people." The closing Hebrew clause (we-anoki lo-ehyeh lakem, literally "and I will not be to you") omits any predicate noun such as "God" and echoes the covenantal name Ehyeh ("I AM") of Exodus 3:14.
notes.2:3: Ammi ("My people") and Ruhamah ("She has been shown compassion") reverse the names Lo-ammi and Lo-ruhamah from chapter 1. Masoretic Hosea 2:1-3 corresponds to 1:10-2:1 in many English Bibles.
notes.2:8: The Masoretic Hebrew shifts abruptly from second-person feminine singular ("your way," darkek) to third-person feminine singular ("her wall ... her paths ... she will not find"); "erect a wall against her" renders a cognate construction literally "wall up her wall."
notes.2:17: Achor means "trouble" (cf. Joshua 7:26). The Qal verb anetah ("she will answer") links to the fivefold "answer" in 2:23-24, though the same root can also mean "sing" (as in Exodus 15:21).
notes.2:18: Hebrew baali means both "my master/husband" and "my Baal," creating a deliberate link to "the names of the Baals" in 2:19 in contrast to ishi ("my husband").
notes.2:21: The preposition be- ("with") with the Piel verb aras ("betroth") idiomatically marks the bride-price paid by the groom (cf. 2 Samuel 3:14); "loyal love" renders Hebrew hesed.
notes.3:1: The Masoretic accents group od ("again") with "Go" rather than with "said to me." The noun rea ("companion") can refer either to an illicit lover or to a woman's own husband.
notes.3:2: The Masoretic text literally reads "fifteen of silver" (with "shekels" implied) and repeats "barley" after lethech, a rare dry measure occurring only here in the Hebrew Bible and traditionally reckoned as half a homer.
notes.3:3: The closing clause (we-gam-ani elayik, literally "and also I toward you") is verbless and elliptical, leaving open whether Hosea vows equal fidelity or mutual abstention during the waiting period.
notes.3:4: Teraphim were household or divinatory cult images (cf. Judges 17:5; Zechariah 10:2) paired here with the priestly ephod.
notes.4:4: The Masoretic Text reads we'ammekha kimrivei khohen ("for your people are like those who dispute with a priest"), using a Hiphil masculine plural construct participle of riv; some modern versions emend the text to read "my dispute is with you, priest."
notes.4:6: The written Ketiv reads w'm's'k with an extra aleph before the pronominal suffix; the translation follows the read Qere we'em'asekha ("and I will reject you"), the standard Qal imperfect 1cs form of ma'as with a 2ms suffix.
notes.4:8: The Hebrew noun chatta't means both "sin" and "sin offering," creating a wordplay on priests eating sacrificial sin offerings while feeding on the people's wrongdoing; the singular suffix on nafsho ("his appetite") is distributive.
notes.4:10: The Masoretic verse division places the infinitive lishmor ("to heed") at the end of verse 10 rather than joining it to the opening nouns of verse 11.
notes.4:18: The clause rendered "her rulers deeply love disgrace" translates the difficult Masoretic wording ahavu hevu qalon maginneha, taking ahavu hevu as an emphatic doubling of "love" (though hevu is sometimes read as the imperative "Give!") and maginneha (literally "her shields") as a metaphor for rulers.
notes.5:2: The Masoretic Text reads shachatah setim he'miqu ("the rebels have plunged deep into slaughter"), using a Hiphil perfect of amaq with setim ("rebels, apostates"); "I am a discipline for all of them" preserves the literal nominal clause using musar ("discipline, correction").
notes.5:7: Hebrew chodesh means either "new moon" (referring to the New Moon festival) or "a month," and chelqehem denotes their allotted portions or tracts of land.
notes.5:11: The rare Hebrew noun tsav (from tsavah, "command") means "precept" or "command," likely referring to unauthorized human or idolatrous decrees; the Septuagint instead reads "vanity."
notes.5:13: The Masoretic Text divides the title as melekh yarev ("King Jareb"), either a symbolic epithet meaning "contending king" (from riv) or a wordplay on the Assyrian royal title "the great king."
notes.6:3: Hebrew yoreh is rendered as a Qal participle ("that soaks/waters," from yarah), though it can also be read as the noun for the autumn (early) rain paired with the spring rain (malqosh).
notes.6:5: The Masoretic Text reads umishpatekha or yetse ("and your judgments are like light going forth," referring to the judgments pronounced against you), whereas the Septuagint divides the consonants differently to read "and My judgment goes forth as light."
notes.6:7: Hebrew ke'adam can be translated either as "like Adam" (referring to the first man) or generically as "like mankind/humans."
notes.6:10: The written Ketiv reads sh'ryryh (with yod instead of waw); the translation follows the read Qere sha'aruriyyah ("an appalling thing" or "a horrible thing").
notes.6:11: The idiom shuv shevut ("restore the fortunes," literally "turn a turning" or "bring back the captivity") closes verse 11 in the Masoretic Text, though some modern versions attach this clause to 7:1.
notes.7:5: Hebrew hehelu is a Hiphil perfect of chalah, taken here in an inchoative sense ('grew sick'), though some parse it transitively ('they made the officials sick'). The construct phrase chamat miyyayin ('heat from wine') places a prepositional phrase directly after a construct noun.
notes.7:6: The Masoretic Text reads qerevu (Piel perfect of qarav, 'brought near') and ofehem ('their baker', continuing the oven metaphor of v. 4); some ancient versions reflect vocalizations meaning 'their inward parts' and 'their anger'.
notes.7:14: Masoretic yitgoraru is a Hithpolel imperfect of gur ('gather together' or 'assemble'). A graphic variant reflected in the Septuagint and some Hebrew manuscripts reads yitgodadu from gadad ('gash themselves').
notes.7:16: Hebrew lo al literally means 'not upward' (or 'not to the height'), often understood as 'not to the Most High'.
notes.8:5: Hebrew zanach is a 3ms Qal perfect ('He has spurned'), deliberately echoing Israel's rejection of what is good in v. 3; others construe it passively ('Your calf is spurned') or link it to a homonymous root meaning 'be foul'.
notes.8:10: Hebrew vayyachellu meat is a difficult Masoretic phrase: vayyachellu is pointed as a Hiphil of chalal ('begin', here with meat, 'few', yielding 'start to grow few'), though some relate it to chul ('writhe') with meat as 'soon'. Hebrew melekh sarim literally reads 'king of officials', an allusion to the Assyrian monarch.
notes.8:12: Ketiv/Qere: the written text (ketiv) reads ekhtov (plene spelling) and ribbo ('ten thousand' or 'a myriad'), while the read text (qere) followed here has ekhtov- (defective spelling) and rubbe ('multitudes' or 'many things'), agreeing with the plural Niphal verb nechshavu ('they are counted').
notes.8:13: Hebrew havhavay ('My offerings') is a hapax legomenon, a reduplicated noun from yahav ('give') with a 1cs suffix.
notes.9:1: The Masoretic Text reads el-gil ('to exultation'), whereas the Septuagint reflects a negative jussive al-tagel ('do not exult').
notes.9:2: The Masoretic Text has a 3fs suffix bah ('her'), referring to Israel personified as an unfaithful wife (v. 1), though several ancient versions harmonize to plural 'them'.
notes.9:8: The opening clause tzofeh Efrayim im-elohay is terse: tzofeh is a Qal active participle ('watchman' or 'watching over') taking Ephraim as its object; some instead render 'Ephraim is a watchman with my God'.
notes.9:13: A famously difficult Masoretic verse: kaasher-raiti leTzor ('just as I saw concerning Tyre') uses le- as a marker of reference, and lehotzi is a Hiphil infinitive construct with le- expressing impending obligation ('must bring out').
notes.9:16: Ketiv/Qere: the written text (ketiv) reads the poetic negative beli, while the read text (qere) followed here has bal; both mean 'not'.
notes.10:1: Hebrew boqeq (Qal participle of baqaq) is understood here as 'spreading/luxuriant' from the context of abundant fruit, though the homonymous root means 'emptying.'
notes.10:2: Hebrew chalaq (Qal perfect) is stative 'is smooth/deceitful' (chalaq II), though some render it 'is divided' (chalaq I); ya'arof (Qal imperfect of araf) literally means 'will break the neck of.'
notes.10:5: MT uses the feminine plural eglot ('calves/heifers') alongside masculine singular suffixes referring to the idol of Beth-aven; yagilu (Qal imperfect of gil) usually means 'rejoice' and is taken here as 'wail/tremble' in grief or ironically as former exultation.
notes.10:6: MT reads le-melekh yarev ('to King Jareb,' perhaps an epithet meaning 'contending king'); some redivide the consonants as malki rav, 'the great king.'
notes.10:10: Translates the Qere onotam ('their iniquities,' contracted plural of awon) rather than the Ketiv eynotam (resembling 'their eyes' or 'their springs'); Hebrew also pairs essorem (Qal imperfect of yasar, 'discipline') with be-osram (Qal infinitive construct of asar, 'bind').
notes.11:3: Hebrew tirgalti is a rare Tiphel perfect (denominative from regel, 'foot') meaning 'taught to walk'; MT shifts to the third person masculine singular in qacham al-zero'otaw ('He took them up in His arms,' with aphaeretic Qal perfect qach for laqach).
notes.11:6: Hebrew baddaw may mean 'his diviners/oracle-priests' (bad II, cf. Jer 50:36) or 'his gate-bars' (bad I).
notes.11:7: A difficult verse in MT: telu'im (Qal passive participle of tala) literally means 'hung/suspended toward,' and yiqra'uhu ('they call him') with el-al ('to the Most High') and Polel yeromem ('exalt') is variously construed.
notes.11:9: Hebrew be'ir is taken as 'in fury/wrath' (ir II, parallel to 'burning anger'); alternatively it means 'into a city' (ir I).
notes.12:1: Hebrew rad (Qal perfect of rud, 'roam restlessly/be unruly') with im-qedoshim ne'eman (plural of majesty 'the Holy One' plus Niphal participle 'faithful') is read here negatively in line with 12:3; others take the clause positively as 'still rules/walks with God and is faithful to the Holy One.'
notes.12:5: MT reads immanu ('with us'), identifying Hosea's generation with Jacob at Bethel; yimtsa'ennu ('He found him') takes God as subject consistently with the following verb, though some read 'he [Jacob] found Him.'
notes.12:8: Hebrew kena'an ('Canaan') is a biting wordplay meaning both 'trader/merchant' and the Canaanite nation.
notes.12:13: Hebrew shamar (Qal perfect of shamar, 'keep/guard/keep watch') has no expressed object here (referring to tending Laban's flocks) and pairs directly with Niphal nishmar ('was watched over/kept') in 12:14.
notes.13:2: The final clause is grammatically difficult; literally "sacrificers of mankind kiss calves," it may also be understood as a partitive construction, "let those among mankind who sacrifice kiss calves."
notes.13:9: The Hebrew is extremely terse, literally "It has ruined you, Israel, for against Me, against your help." The third-person singular Piel verb takes Israel's rebellion as its implied subject, with the repeated preposition marking apposition ("against Me, your helper").
notes.13:14: The opening clauses lack an interrogative marker in Hebrew and may alternatively be read declaratively ("I will ransom them... I will redeem them..."). The rare form rendered "Where" here and in v. 10 functions as an interrogative adverb rather than the verb "I will be," and the noun rendered "destruction" denotes deadly blight or plague.
notes.13:15: The verb "flourishes" is a Hiphil form of the root for bearing fruit spelled with an aleph, forming a wordplay on the name Ephraim. The masculine pronoun "It" resumes the east wind of the LORD, though it may also allude to the invading power or to the LORD Himself.
notes.14:3: The Masoretic Text reads "bulls" with "our lips" in apposition, portraying spoken repentance and praise offered in place of bull sacrifices. Ancient versions divide the Hebrew consonants differently to read "the fruit of our lips."
notes.14:8: The Piel verb literally means "keep alive" or "make grow," taking "grain" directly as its object without a comparative "like." The singular suffix in "his shadow" continues the metaphor of Israel as the flourishing tree of vv. 6-7, though some take it to refer to the LORD.
notes.14:9: Many interpreters read the opening question as spoken by repentant Ephraim, to which the LORD replies in the following clauses. The Hebrew shifts from third person ("watch over him") to second person ("your fruit"), a common poetic device in Hosea.
